text.p: Portuguese bonds closed at their day's lows in nervous trade and dealers said prices could fall further on Wednesday as concern grows over a possible delay to the launch of Europe's single currency.

"Nervous, nervous and even more nervous was how things were today. Even though the 10-year bond yield didn't go through seven percent, it could easily do so tomorrow if Spanish prices drop further," said one trader.
Dealers said fears that the euro's launch may be delayed if Germany is unable to meet the single currency criteria together with the prospect of a rise in U.S. rates had undermined prices.
"Added to this bleak scenario are rising money market rates and the weakness of the peseta which has had a knock-on effect on the escudo. The whole yield curve is fragile," said another dealer.
Currency traders said that the Bank of Portugal had intervened discreetly to support the escudo. It closed at 100.69/72 per mark compared with an opening 100.59/62.
